brain-dump.headline: Say it once, and let it sort itself out
brain-dump.summary: BrainDump lets you capture unstructured notes by typing or by speaking, and can use AI to turn them into journal summaries, mood tags, and task lists. Notes can be saved on your device without an account; an account is required for anything that leaves your device — syncing, AI processing, and shared notebooks.
brain-dump.audience: For anyone who thinks faster than they can organise, and would rather empty their head first and tidy it later.

features.title: Type it or say it
features.body: Dictate a note or write it. Voice recognition runs on your own device, and it is free and unlimited on every tier.

features.title: AI does the tidying
features.body: Turn a pile of notes into a daily journal summary, mood tags, and an extracted task list.

features.title: Shared notebooks
features.body: Invite other people into a notebook when something is worth keeping together rather than alone.

faq.q: How much does it cost?
faq.a: Writing, saving, and dictating notes are free and unlimited. The free tier is supported by advertising and includes a limited number of free AI summaries. Premium removes the ads and the summary limit, and adds notebook invitations and a larger watchlist.

faq.q: Do I need an account?
faq.a: Not to write notes — those can be saved on the device on their own. An account is needed for anything that leaves the device: syncing, AI processing, and shared notebooks.

faq.q: How do I cancel my subscription?
faq.a: Manage it in your Apple App Store or Google Play account settings. Subscriptions are billed by the store, not by us.

faq.q: How do I export or delete my data?
faq.a: Open Settings, then "Export account data" for a JSON copy, or "Delete account" to permanently remove everything.

faq.q: The AI didn't work.
faq.a: AI processing is a premium feature, with a few free trial runs. Check your internet connection and try again from the Today screen.

brain-dump.disclaimer: BrainDump is not a medical, mental-health, legal, or financial service. AI-generated output may be inaccurate or incomplete — review it before relying on it.

termsSections.title: Who we are
paragraphs: BrainDump is provided by Emily Xiong, a sole trader based in Ontario, Canada ("we", "us"). You can reach us at xiongemi@gmail.com.

termsSections.title: Eligibility
paragraphs: You must be at least 13 years old to use the app, or older where your country sets a higher minimum age for consenting to online services. The app is not directed at children.

termsSections.title: The service
paragraphs: BrainDump lets you capture unstructured notes by typing or by speaking, and can use AI to turn them into journal summaries, mood tags, and task lists. The service is provided "as is" without warranties of any kind. AI-generated output may be inaccurate or incomplete — review it before relying on it. BrainDump is not a medical, mental-health, legal, or financial service.
Notes can be saved on your device without an account. An account is required for anything that leaves your device — syncing, AI processing, and shared notebooks.

termsSections.title: Your account
paragraphs: You are responsible for activity under your account and for the content you submit. Do not use the app for unlawful purposes or to submit content you do not have the right to submit.

termsSections.title: Your content
paragraphs: You keep ownership of everything you write. You grant us only the permission needed to operate the service for you: to store your content, transmit it to the providers listed in our privacy policy, and display it back to you and to anyone you have deliberately shared it with. We do not use your content to train AI models.

termsSections.title: Shared notebooks
paragraphs: A notebook can be shared with other people by invitation. You should treat anything placed in a shared notebook as visible to every member of that notebook.
bullets: Members can read every note in a notebook, and can add their own.
Only a note's author can edit or delete that note.
The notebook owner can remove members or delete the notebook. Deleting a notebook does not delete the notes inside it; they become unfiled for their authors.
You are responsible for what you place in a shared notebook and for who you invite. Anyone holding a valid invite link can join until that link is revoked.
Creating a notebook is free. Inviting other people to one is a Premium feature.

termsSections.title: Watched pages
paragraphs: You can ask the app to watch a public web page — typically an annual event's own website — for signs that new dates have been announced. If you do:
bullets: Our servers will retrieve that page on a recurring schedule that you choose, until you remove it from your watchlist.
Only pages that are publicly reachable can be watched. Some sites block automated readers; those cannot be watched and the app will say so.
When a page appears to have changed, its visible text may be sent to our AI provider to read dates out of it.
Add only pages you have a legitimate reason to monitor, and do not use this feature in a way that breaches a site's own terms.
Detected dates are a convenience, not a guarantee. Confirm them with the organiser before relying on them.

termsSections.title: Links you save
paragraphs: When you save a note containing a web address, our servers may retrieve that page to show you a preview of it — its title, description, and image. Only the address you saved is used.

termsSections.title: Calendar access
paragraphs: If you choose to add a detected event to your calendar, the app asks your device for calendar permission and writes a single event. It does not read, alter, or transmit your existing calendar entries. You can withdraw the permission at any time in your device settings.

termsSections.title: Subscriptions
bullets: BrainDump Premium is offered as a monthly or annual auto-renewing subscription.
Payment is charged to your Apple App Store or Google Play account at confirmation of purchase.
Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Manage or cancel in your App Store / Play Store account settings.
Prices are shown in the app before purchase and may vary by region.

termsSections.title: Free tier and advertising
paragraphs: The free tier is supported by advertisements and includes a limited number of free AI summaries. Writing and saving notes, and dictating them with your voice, are free and unlimited on every tier — voice recognition runs on your own device.
Premium adds:
bullets: Unlimited AI summaries, task extraction, and mood tracking, once your free summaries are used up.
No advertisements.
The ability to invite other people to a shared notebook.
A larger watchlist.

termsSections.title: Refunds
paragraphs: Purchases are processed by Apple or Google, not by us, and refunds are handled under their policies. Request a refund through your App Store or Google Play account. Where consumer law in your country grants you a right of withdrawal, that right still applies.

termsSections.title: Termination
paragraphs: You may stop using the app and delete your account at any time from Settings. Deleting your account removes your entries, tasks, saved links, notebooks, and watchlist from our servers. We may suspend or terminate access for violations of these terms.

termsSections.title: Limitation of liability
paragraphs: To the maximum extent permitted by law, we are not liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the app. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited under the law that applies to you, including your statutory rights as a consumer.

termsSections.title: Apple
paragraphs: If you obtained the app from the Apple App Store: these terms are between you and us, not Apple. Apple is not responsible for the app or its content and has no obligation to provide support or maintenance for it. Apple and its subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of these terms and may enforce them against you.

termsSections.title: Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of the Province of Ontario and the federal laws of Canada that apply there, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. If you are a consumer resident elsewhere, you keep the protection of any mandatory consumer law of your own country, and may bring proceedings in your own courts where that law allows.

termsSections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We may update these terms. If a change is material we will ask you to accept the updated terms in the app before you continue to use it. Otherwise, continued use after changes constitutes acceptance.

termsSections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Email xiongemi@gmail.com.

privacySections.title: Who is responsible for your data
paragraphs: BrainDump is provided by Emily Xiong, a sole trader based in Ontario, Canada, who is the controller of the personal data described here. Contact: xiongemi@gmail.com.

privacySections.title: Information we collect
bullets: Account information — when you sign in with Google or Apple, our authentication provider (Clerk) gives us your user identifier and email address.

Content you create — the text and voice-dictated notes you write ("brain dumps"), the AI-generated journal summaries and mood tags, and the tasks you save. These are stored in our database (Supabase) and tied to your account.
Voice — voice notes are transcribed to text on your device using your operating system's speech recognition. We store the resulting text, not the audio.
Subscription status — whether you have an active premium subscription, managed through RevenueCat and the Apple App Store / Google Play.
Usage and diagnostics — anonymised analytics and crash reports (PostHog) to keep the app working, and advertising identifiers for free-tier ads (Google AdMob).

Session recordings — PostHog records anonymised replays of how the app is used (taps, screens, timing) to help us find bugs and confusing screens. All text you type and all images are masked before the recording leaves your device, so the content of your brain dumps is never captured.

privacySections.title: AI processing
paragraphs: AI processing is optional and is never automatic. When you tap "Process with AI", the text of that brain dump is sent to our AI provider (DeepSeek) to generate a summary, a mood tag, and a task list. Only the text you submit for processing is sent — never your account details. Your use of this feature is also subject to the AI provider's own privacy terms.

privacySections.title: Links, watched pages, and your calendar
paragraphs: Three features cause our servers to reach out to the wider internet on your behalf. None of them run unless you start them.
bullets: Link previews — saving a note that contains a web address makes our server retrieve that page so it can show you a title, description, and image. Only the address you saved is sent.

Watched pages — a page you add to your watchlist is retrieved by our server on the schedule you choose, until you remove it. When it appears to have changed, its visible text is sent to our AI provider so dates can be read out of it.

Calendar — adding a detected event asks your device for calendar permission and writes one event locally. Your existing calendar is never read, altered, or transmitted, and the permission can be withdrawn in your device settings.

privacySections.title: How we use your information
bullets: To provide the core features: storing your entries, generating summaries and tasks, and syncing them to your account.
To manage your subscription and, for free users, to show advertisements.
To diagnose crashes and understand aggregate usage so we can improve the app.

privacySections.title: Third-party services
paragraphs: The app relies on these providers, each with its own privacy policy:
bullets: Clerk (authentication)
Supabase (database and storage)
DeepSeek (AI processing)
RevenueCat (subscriptions)
Google AdMob (ads, free tier only)
PostHog (analytics, crash reporting, and masked session replay)

privacySections.title: Data retention and deletion
paragraphs: We keep your data for as long as your account exists. You can permanently delete your account and all associated entries and tasks at any time from Settings → Delete account.
You may also export a full copy of your data as a .json file from Settings → Export account data. To request deletion by email, contact us below.

privacySections.title: Children
paragraphs: The app is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their data.

privacySections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We may update this policy; continued use after changes constitutes acceptance. Material changes will be reflected on this page.

privacySections.title: Contact
paragraphs: Questions about privacy? Email xiongemi@gmail.com.

mend-breakup.headline: A no-contact companion that does not shame you for slipping
mend-breakup.summary: Mend is a 90-day no-contact tracker for the weeks after a breakup. Most breakup apps run on toxic positivity or streaks that reset to zero. Mend keeps every entry on your device and treats a slip as data rather than failure.
mend-breakup.audience: For anyone going no-contact after a breakup who wants an honest, private record of how it is actually going.

features.title: Ninety days, one at a time
features.body: Follow a 90-day no-contact goal without a counter that punishes you for a bad night.

features.title: A slip is data, not a reset
features.body: Log the times you reached out and read the pattern, instead of starting again from zero.

features.title: Private by design
features.body: Entries are stored on your device. There is no account to create and nothing to sync.

faq.q: Does anything I write leave my phone?
faq.a: Your entries are kept on the device itself. There is no account and no copy on a server.

faq.q: Is Mend a substitute for therapy?
faq.a: No. It is a self-help tool for tracking your own progress. If you are struggling, please speak to a qualified professional.

mend-breakup.disclaimer: Mend is a self-help tool. It is not therapy, counselling, or a mental-health service, and it does not provide medical advice. If you are in crisis, contact your local emergency number or a crisis line in your country.

job-tracker-util.summary: Job Tracker Util keeps every application in one list. Add a role in seconds, update its status when something moves, and get on with your day. Nothing is uploaded, because there is nowhere for it to go.
job-tracker-util.audience: For anyone running a job search across more roles than they can keep in their head.

features.title: Add a role in seconds
features.body: Enough detail to be useful, few enough fields that logging an application is never a chore.

features.title: Status, updated when it changes
features.body: Move an application along as you hear back, and see where everything stands at a glance.

features.title: Your search stays yours
features.body: Applications live on the device. No sign-in, no server, no career history in somebody else's cloud.

faq.q: Is my job search data uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Applications are stored on your device only.

faq.q: Does the app apply to jobs for me?
faq.a: No. It is a record-keeping tool. You apply, it remembers.

job-tracker-util.disclaimer: Job Tracker Util is a personal record-keeping tool. It is not affiliated with any job board, recruiter, or employer, and it does not submit applications on your behalf.

dementia-daily-memory-test.headline: Two-minute memory exercises, made to feel good to finish
dementia-daily-memory-test.summary: Short, calm memory exercises for people living with dementia and the people caring for them. No timers and no score to lose, so a session ends on an encouraging note rather than a clinical one.
dementia-daily-memory-test.audience: For people living with memory loss, and for the family members and caregivers sitting beside them.

features.title: Two minutes, start to finish
features.body: Short enough to complete in one sitting, on whatever schedule suits the day.

features.title: Calm and encouraging by design
features.body: No countdown timers, no streaks, and no score that can be lost.

features.title: Alone or together
features.body: Built to work independently, and to work just as well with a caregiver alongside.

faq.q: Does this diagnose dementia?
faq.a: No. It is an exercise app, not a screening or diagnostic tool. Talk to a doctor about any concern with memory.

faq.q: Is it on Android?
faq.a: Yes. Daily Memory Test is available on both the App Store and Google Play.

dementia-daily-memory-test.disclaimer: Daily Memory Test is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, monitor, or screen for dementia or any other condition, and it is not a substitute for advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
